extracted.intended_audience: researchers, research administrators, partners and the general public interested in CNRS research priorities and standards
extracted.subtask_description: Institutional statement of CNRS standards and expectations for research practice and evaluation, covering societal benefit, interdisciplinarity, partnerships, assessment, scientific integrity, innovation and the role of ethical oversight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research must deliver benefit to society
rubrics_metrics.description: Research must deliver benefit. It must benefit society. It should help humanity to progress. It must share knowledge and innovate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To achieve this, the CNRS has chosen to pursue research that leverages every field, in pursuit of sustainable progress, to deliver technological, scientific or societal advances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multidisciplinarity
rubrics_metrics.description: Since it explores all fields of science, research at the CNRS is intrinsically multidisciplinary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research spans every field and is expected to be multidisciplinary (see CNRS disciplines).

rubrics_metrics.name: Partnerships and long-lasting collaboration
rubrics_metrics.description: Bringing stakeholders together, founding partnerships, fostering the conditions for a long-lasting collaboration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CNRS promotes stakeholder engagement and durable partnerships as a key condition for successful research and its societal uptake.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment and evaluation as the basis of credibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The credibility and legitimacy of public research is grounded above all in evaluation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Robust evaluation processes are presented as essential to validate and legitimize public research activity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collective scientific expertise to inform public decision-making
rubrics_metrics.description: Institutional scientific expertise aims to enlighten public decision making and debates relating to major societal issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The CNRS provides collective expertise intended to inform policy and public debate on major societal challenges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research responding to global and societal challenges
rubrics_metrics.description: Research responding to the world's challenges: The CNRS as a stakeholder is fully committed to the life of the community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research priorities are framed to address major global challenges and demonstrate commitment to community and societal needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research driving innovation and technology transfer
rubrics_metrics.description: Innovative inventions, technologies and businesses: the spark of innovation begins in laboratories conducting basic research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Basic research is positioned as the source of inventions, technologies and business creation; fostering translation from lab discoveries to innovation is an explicit objective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific integrity, deontology and ethics as foundational values
rubrics_metrics.description: Scientific Integrity at the CNRS: Scientific integrity is one of the founding principles of the CNRS. At the CNRS, the values of deontology, scientific integrity, and ethics are fundamental and constitute the foundation of our responsibility in terms of research and innovation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Integrity is operationalised through the Mission for Scientific Integrity (MIS) and the CNRS’s Scientific Integrity Officer; these bodies deliver the rules and values that guarantee research credibility and public trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics Officer responsibilities and legal basis
rubrics_metrics.description: The role of Ethics Officer derives from the law dated April 20th 2016 on ethics and the rights and obligations of civil servants and its implementing decree in April 2017. The Ethics Officer is legally responsible for responding to requests for advice from civil servants on ethics and more specifically on integrity, probity, neutrality, secularity, professional secrecy, the independence of researchers, hierarchical obedience, occupying more than one job and conflicts of interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ethical oversight includes providing advice on a wide range of integrity-related issues (neutrality, secularity, professional secrecy, independence, conflicts of interest, moonlighting, hierarchical obedience) backed by legal mandate.
